Jacob —

Thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below; I pulled in Grace (Lead TAM for banking) and Tessa (on-call operations) so we can add operational detail and roster. High-level: we operate a blended model (TAM-led coordination + engineering bridge handoff). Details follow.

1) Bridge model:
- Redwood provides a TAM-led incident bridge during business hours (08:00–18:00 local business days). The TAM coordinates and keeps the customer bridge open.
- For after-hours Sev1s, our on-call engineer (rotation managed by ops) will open the engineering bridge and the assigned TAM will join within the first 30 minutes to coordinate stakeholder comms.
- For critical outages that meet your Sev1 definition, we commit a targeted join time of 15 minutes for the on-call engineer and 30 minutes for the TAM (measured from our alerting system).

2) Notification windows (suggested ladder):
- Sev1 (production down / data loss):
  * 0–15m: paging to on-call engineer (SMS + phone)
  * 0–30m: on-call engineer joins bridge; TAM paged
  * 0–60m: Incident Manager (customer-facing TAM) notifies primary incident contact and incident manager at First Horizon
  * 60–120m: Exec sponsor notification (if incident remains Sev1)
- Sev2 (partial degradation):
  * 0–60m: TAM alerted and opens a bridge; on-call engineer paged if needed
  * 4 hours: broader stakeholder update if unresolved
- Sev3 (minor, non-customer facing):
  * Regular business hours resolution; weekly summary if recurring

3) Templates and roster: attached are three items we typically share — an editable notify template (support-incident-notify-template.docx), the TAM+on-call roster with shift windows (fh_tam_roster.xlsx), and our SLA exhibit (redwood-sla-exhibit.pdf). Please review and we can adapt to your escalation labels.

Operational notes / handoff expectations:
- We recommend you publish a single incident manager and an exec sponsor in your runbook; TAMs will use those exact contacts for 60–120 minute escalations.
- We run a weekly on-call sync so the roster reflects planned shifts; we can provide an API export for automation if you want direct pull.

Grace or Tessa — would you add the bridge dialing matrix and the engineer rotation details?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: support-incident-notify-template.docx, fh_tam_roster.xlsx, redwood-sla-exhibit.pdf

Adding the operational bridge details and routing matrix below. I kept items concise so your Ops team can drop them in the runbook.

Bridge dialing matrix (example):
- Customer bridge (Redwood-hosted): dial-in URL + PIN (we will provision unique for First Horizon)
- Engineering bridge (after-hours): +1-415-555-0102 (rotating endpoint) / participant PIN xxxxx
- Backchannel Slack (optional): #fh-production-incidents (we can create and invite)

On-call rotation highlights (what you can expect):
- Primary on-call engineer: 24/7 pager rotation (4 teams). When pager fires: engineer answers within 15 minutes, triages, and determines bridge requirement.
- TAM coverage:
  * Business hours (08:00–18:00 ET): assigned TAM staffed and will open the customer bridge.
  * After hours: TAM is on-call but will join remote (within 30 minutes) while engineers own the initial bridge.

Escalation ladder (First Horizon naming):
1) Primary Incident Contact at First Horizon (customer) — immediate updates
2) First Horizon Incident Manager (customer) — 60m escalation
3) Redwood TAM (Grace O'Connor) — continuous coordination
4) Redwood On-call Engineering Lead (rotating) — technical resolution
5) Redwood Director on-call (Karthik Iyer) — exec escalation if >4 hours

Templates: use the attached notify template. Example subject lines we recommend: "[FH] Sev1: production incident — short summary". In the body include JIRA/Case ID, impact summary, mitigation steps, and next update ETA.

I'll follow up with the roster export (CSV) and a short runbook snippet you can paste into your internal docs.
